newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end strong week with another high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end strong week with another high.

text.p: Swiss shares ended this week's relentless record run with with another high, jumping more than one percent on favourable U.S. job data, a rising U.S. dollar and a strong Wall Street opening.
Investors, who have been increasingly attracted to the Swiss market after recent recommendations by U.S. and British brokers, had a particular liking for for drug companies and banks.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 48.1 points, or 1.12 percent, at 4,357.9, a shade off the all-time high of 4,362.5.
The all-share SPI was up 29.86 points, or 1.08 percent, to 2,783.25, after setting a new high of 2,783.59.
Dealers said there were no real alternative to shares given the relatively low level of bond yields.

Bank shares were increasingly in demand as the creation of a Holocaust memorial fund by the major three banks improved sentiment, a trader noted. One dealer also cited the growing belief that the high level of write-downs, which put gains of several banks under pressure in the past few years, may be a thing of the past.
CS Group jumped 2.5 francs to 151. SBC and UBS also posted solid gains.
Most-active Novartis registered shares were up 16 francs, or nearly one percent, at 1,693. Roche certificates recovered from Thursday's profit taking, climbing 205 francs to 12,190.
Dollar-sensitive Surveillance, SMH, and Holderbank showed solid gains. Swissair powered ahead 60 francs to 1,335.
Temporary labour firm Adecco jumped 20 francs, or more than five percent, to 408 on an upgrade by a foreign broker
Sulzer and Clariant were slightly lower, consolidating recent advances. ABB and Alusuisse underperformed the market but still ended slightly higher.
